packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02: UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context gave a proposed identification of this
packet before I read it. However, while reading I recognised the wording of
both columns on the main face, and of the second strip, as familiar Latin
(scriptural-sounding) phrasing. I did not use that recognition to fill gaps:
anything I could not see is marked [illegible] or given with "?". I have not
named a work or author. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (I opened only
PROMPT.md and the 13 images; packet.json not read).

All 13 images loaded.

------------------------------------------------------------------
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
------------------------------------------------------------------
image-001: one full face of a parchment leaf, landscape-wise, reused as a limp
  cover or wrapper. Two columns of a formal gothic textualis, 16 lines visible
  per column, ruled in drypoint/plummet. Red touches on initials (S? in col a
  line 1; E in line 7; I in lines 12 and 14). No running title visible. No
  interlinear glosses. One later cursive note, 3 lines, in the right margin
  beside col b (see image-007). At the bottom a folded-over turn-in strip
  carries text upside down relative to the main face, with a vertical red bar
  (rubricated initial stroke?). Bottom of both columns is partly covered by
  this turn-in and by a loose flap.
image-004: the same face rotated 180 degrees (same text, upside down); the
  turn-in strip at top now reads upright. Overlap only, not extra text.
image-002: native-resolution crop of col a of image-001 (lines 1-16).
image-003: native-resolution crop of col b of image-001 (lines 1-16).
image-005, image-006: close-ups of the turn-in strip (upright), from image-004
  top right and top left.
image-007: close-up of the cursive marginal note.
image-008 to image-011: photographs of a DIFFERENT parchment piece, a strip
  used inside a limp binding (held open by hand; a paper text block in later
  German-looking cursive behind it, not part of this reading). Same kind of
  textualis, one column fully readable (right in image-008), the other column
  mostly lost to staining/delamination (image-010).
image-012, image-013: close-ups of the inner cover/lining under that strip:
  horizontal ruled lines in sets with black marks resembling note heads and
  stems (looks like musical notation on staves, or possibly pen trials). Not
  transcribed beyond description; the marks are too sparse to read.

Tentative interpretation: a biblical-style continuous text in two columns, no
commentary or gloss visible. Text in col a and col b is continuous prose; col b
probably does not directly follow col a (different subject matter), so the two
columns may not be consecutive, or text is lost between them. I cannot tell
recto/verso from these images.

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. TRANSCRIPTION: main face, column a (image-002; same lines in image-001
   left column and image-004 inverted right column)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Abbreviations kept where visible; expansions in ( ).

image-002 l.1  tabo illas. [S? red touched]icut uisitat pas
image-002 l.2  tor gregem su[u?](m) in die quando   ["su..." faded]
image-002 l.3  fu(er)it in medio ouiu(m) suar(um) dissi
image-002 l.4  pata(rum)? : sic uisitabo oues meas
image-002 l.5  & lib(er)abo eas de omnib(us) locis in
image-002 l.6  quib(us) disp(er)se fuera(n)t. in die nu
image-002 l.7  bis & caliginis. [E, red touched]t educam
image-002 l.8  eas de p(o)p(u)lis. et (con)gregabo eas
image-002 l.9  de t(er)ris: et inducā(m) eas i(n) t(er)ram   ["de" faded]
image-002 l.10 suam. et pascā(m) eas in montib(us)
image-002 l.11 isr(ae)l. in riuis in cunctis [s?]edib(us)
image-002 l.12 t(er)re. [I, red touched]n pascuis uberrimis pascā(m)
image-002 l.13 eas: et in montib(us) excelsis isr(ae)l
image-002 l.14 erū(n)t pascue ea(rum). [I, red touched]bi requiescē(n)t
image-002 l.15 in herbis uirentib(us): & in pascu
image-002 l.16 is pinguib(us) pascent(ur) sup(er) mō(n)[...]   [lower half cut off at
               bottom edge of image-002; visible complete in image-001]

Note l.14: "eaR(um)" has a heavier dark-ink retouch over "ea(rum)".
Note l.11: initial "s" of "[s?]edibus" is not clearly visible; "edib(us)" is.
Bottom of col a below l.16 is covered by the turn-in strip.

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. TRANSCRIPTION: main face, column b (image-003; same lines image-001 right
   column, image-004 inverted left column)
------------------------------------------------------------------
image-003 l.1  [ma?]iestate sua. & om(n)es angeli [ei?]us   [first letters faded]
image-003 l.2  cum eo: tu(n)c sedebit sup(er) sedem
image-003 l.3  maiestatis sue. Et (con)gregabu(n)t(ur)
image-003 l.4  ante eu(m) om(n)es gentes: et separabit
image-003 l.5  eos ab inuice(m). sicut pastor segre
image-003 l.6  gat oues ab edis. Et statuet
image-003 l.7  oues quide(m) a dextris suis: edos
image-003 l.8  aut(em) a sinistris. Tunc [d?]icet re[x?]   [red blot over "dicet"]
image-003 l.9  hiis qui a dextris eius erunt.
image-003 l.10 Venite benedicti p(at)ris mei: possi
image-003 l.11 dete paratu(m) uobis regnu(m) a con
image-003 l.12 stitucione mundi. Esuriui eni(m)
image-003 l.13 et dedistis michi manducare.
image-003 l.14 Sitiui et dedistis michi bibere.   [large S; "dedistis" faded]
image-003 l.15 Hospes eram: et collegistis me   ["me" partly under loose flap]
image-003 l.16 [N?][...] [covered by flap] [...]am in sil[...]   [only fragments visible]

Above l.10 a small dark-ink mark (caret or correction sign) between "mei" and
"possi". Line l.1 begins mid-word, so the column continues from a lost line.

------------------------------------------------------------------
4. TURN-IN STRIP (image-005, image-006; inverted in image-001 bottom)
------------------------------------------------------------------
image-005 l.1  [illegible, faded, top cut]
image-005 l.2  [q?]uam dum i(n)ueniri potest: in   [red vertical bar at left; "q" uncertain,
               could be "d"]
image-005 l.3  (upside-down) is pinguib(us) pascent(ur) sup(er) mo[...]
               - this is the inverted bottom line of col a (= image-002 l.16), not
               new text.
image-006 l.1  [illegible] [...]mus? [faded, cut]
image-006 l.2  [...]hii? in supplicu(m)? et(er)nu(m)?   ["hii" uncertain; final mark ":"
               or "?"-like punctus]
Relationship of this strip to the main columns (whether same leaf folded, or
a separate piece) cannot be determined from these images.

------------------------------------------------------------------
5. MARGINAL NOTE beside col b (image-007; image-001 right margin)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Later cursive, brown/grey ink, vernacular-looking, very uncertain:
image-007 l.1  [illegible] [...]ischr? di[...]
image-007 l.2  Du nar m[in?]  [with a small caret/insertion mark above between "nar" and "m"]
image-007 l.3  Du(n)? [s?]prim? bal[...]
Right edge cut by the fold of the cover.

------------------------------------------------------------------
6. SECOND PARCHMENT STRIP in binding (image-009 best; same in image-008 right
   column and image-011 rotated)
------------------------------------------------------------------
image-009 l.1  [stain]  [ue?]n[ir?]e. Et dicebat ei[s?]
image-009 l.2  Vos deorsum estis: ego de su[...]  [line end abbreviated, unclear]
image-009 l.3  nis? sum. Vos de mundo ho[c?]
image-009 l.4  estis: ego nō(n) sum de hoc mu(n)
image-009 l.5  do. Dixi ego? [ergo?] uobis: q(ui)a morie
image-009 l.6  mini in p(e)cc(at)is u(est)ris. Si enim
image-009 l.7  nō(n) credide[r]itis q(ui)a ego [sum?]   [bottom line, cut by curl]

Left column of the same strip (image-010; image-008 left) - line ends only,
heavily stained and delaminated:
image-010 l.1  [illegible] [...]etul? +
image-010 l.2  [illegible] [...]nem tu
image-010 l.3  [illegible] [...] tibi quod
image-010 l.4  [illegible] [...]ōum? 
image-010 l.5  [illegible] [...]a
image-010 l.6  [illegible] [...]ep? [...]
The rest of this column is lost to staining and surface loss.
image-013 lower left shows a further edge of the strip with "[...]ist / [...]ol"
fragments (inverted), not readable as words.

------------------------------------------------------------------
7. LIMITATIONS AND SUGGESTIONS
------------------------------------------------------------------
- Main face: lines below l.16 in both columns are hidden by the turn-in and a
  loose flap; the other side of the wrapper leaf (inside of the cover) is not
  shown in this packet. A photo of the inner face, and of the turn-in unfolded,
  would add text.
- Faded first letters at col a l.2-3 and col b l.1; red-touched initials read
  partly by shape.
- Second strip: only ~7 lines per column visible; the strip is curled, so line
  ends at right are foreshortened. A flat photo of both sides would help.
- image-012/013 staff-like ruling with black marks: description only.
- Column order on the main face is as shown (a left, b right); I cannot tell
  whether col b follows col a directly; the content suggests a gap.
